neighbours.label: the word that introduces an example: ' example' / ' instance' after 'For', ' as' after 'such'
fire: Some birds cannot fly at all. For example, the ostrich relies on its strong legs instead.
Many fruits are rich in vitamin C. For instance, a single orange covers most of a day's needs.
The city has several old bridges, such as the stone one near the cathedral.
Some verbs are irregular in English. For example, the past tense of go is went.
Small habits add up over time. For instance, walking ten minutes a day improves sleep.
Cold climates suit hardy crops such as rye, barley and potatoes.
Prime numbers have no other divisors. For example, seven can only be divided by one and itself.
Several metals conduct heat very well, for instance copper and aluminium.
quiet: Some birds cannot fly at all. The ostrich relies on its strong legs instead.
Many fruits are rich in vitamin C. A single orange covers most of a day's needs.
The city has several old bridges, and the stone one near the cathedral is oldest.
Some verbs are irregular in English. The past tense of go is went.
Small habits add up over time. Walking ten minutes a day improves sleep.
Cold climates suit hardy crops, and rye grows well in the north.
Prime numbers have no other divisors. Seven can only be divided by one and itself.
Several metals conduct heat very well, and copper is widely used in pans.

notes: card: ' example' x15, ' instance', ' as' (such as), Russian 'например'; promotes ' example', ' such'
